issues.description: Method singFarmSongVerse: the problem statement (UML) expects a helper method singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). In the template (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java) the method is declared as private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/) — the parameter is commented out so the template's signature has no formal parameter. The solution (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java) implements protected void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). Because the template's signature omits the Animal parameter, a student implementing singFarmSong() that iterates animals and calls singFarmSongVerse(animal) will get a compilation error against the provided template. This is a real structural mismatch that will block students.
issues.suggestedFix: Restore the Animal parameter in the template method signature so it matches the UML and the solution. Change the template declaration to: private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) { ... } and update the method body to use the animal parameter. This ensures calls like singFarmSongVerse(animal) from singFarmSong() compile for students.

issues.description: Method singFarmSongVerse visibility: the problem statement UML and the template declare singFarmSongVerse as a private helper, while the solution implements it as protected. This inconsistency between the specified UML/template (private) and the provided solution (protected) may confuse students about the intended access level of the helper method and about whether subclasses or tests are expected to access it.
issues.suggestedFix: Make visibility consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution method to private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) to match the UML/template, or (B) update the problem statement and template to document the method as protected if broader access is intended (for example, to allow testing or subclass reuse). Prefer making the visibility explicit in the problem text so students know which access level to implement.
